sections.title: SEIKO_EPSON SEIKO
sections.overview: "A record player developed jointly with Seiko Epson by Mr. Teragaki of Teragaki Research Institute.With the aim of creating a player that is as close as possible to a perfect transducer, we have developed it from the viewpoint of clarification of the fulcrum, and have realized an extremely accurate player that can be called a ""surface roughness meter"".The   2000 was announced as a low-cost model of the   5000 announced in 1994, and 50 units were produced twice each.The bearing structure is such that the main shaft, which is inclined at 1.5  , leans against two disks. The bearing is operated so that the clearance is always 0 caused by the thickness of the oil film.The main spindle is made of SKS steel with hard chrome plating and high-precision polishing. The contact width of the disk is less than 1 mm and the contact area is reduced as much as possible. In addition, by slightly reducing the hardness of the disk, the finished surface of the main spindle is transferred as you use it, and the SN ratio is improved.The lower part of the main shaft is a point structure with carbide balls, and it is designed to transmit the wave motion of the turntable without modulation with minimum friction.The turntable is finished by a high-precision lathe after sufficient annealing of the extruded brass material. No plating or coating process has been applied in consideration of sound quality. The top surface is in the shape of a Hachigata with an inclination of 1.5  , and the inclination of the main shaft is completely cancelled at the position where the needle tip traces.In addition, by using a stabilizer, the record is pressed against the turntable and a stable set is realized.The cross section of the turntable is specially designed to prevent standing waves from occurring.The main shaft and turntable are not simply fitted but firmly integrated by flange connection with four screws, and the weight is about 8 kg.The tone arm uses a static balance system. The weight of the head is more than 300g, and the reference position of the cartridge is stabilized. If this structure is used in a general static balance system, a balance weight of more than 2 kg is required, and the inertia in the horizontal direction becomes too large for smooth operation. However, in   2000, two levers are used, and the balance is balanced with a light weight by the difference in the lever ratio.Each supporting point of the arm has a structure in which contact pressure is always applied in one direction, and smooth operation is achieved.A rod of high tensile steel is incorporated in the arm beam, and rigidity is increased by applying strong compressive stress.The turntable is driven by a unique method using a newly developed coreless brushless motor.When the motor rotates, the idler rotates while biting into the turntable, and automatically rotates at the most stable position to transmit torque at high efficiency."
